answer: Make entry cost a burn of a fixed-supply token traded on an open market. One honest agent buys and burns a single unit cheaply. A farm must buy a thousand at once, and that mass purchase moves the price against itself: as the order book thins, each additional head costs more than the last. The raven-black spike of buy pressure is itself a public signal, a plume of smoke above the farm, and the marginal cost curves up until minting the next fake exceeds anything a fake could ever earn.
